verdicts.reasoning: Addition is the operation in all ten, expressed three different ways — a bare sentence 510 + 1178 in seed 11, a 'What is 5506 + 4430' question in seed 57, and a part-part-whole bond in seed 91 where two parts 5379 and 4200 must be joined. No subtraction or other operation intrudes.

The addends are whole numbers of the size this competency implies: seed 11 pairs a three-digit 510 with a four-digit 1178, while seeds 64 and 127 pair two four-digit numbers. There are no decimals, fractions or units attached, which matches the bare 'numbers' wording.

I totalled every sample: the sums run 1688, 6959, 7779, 9936, 8823, 7808, 9579, 9897, 8776, 9988, so all sit under 10 000 and several press right against the ceiling — 9988 in seed 127, 9897 in seed 103, 9936 in seed 57. The stated bound is both respected and actually exercised near its top.

Read in its competency context, 'with' names the regrouping-required half of the pair, and no sample belongs to it. Column by column, not one of the ten additions produces a column total of ten or more — e.g. 4244 + 4532 gives 6, 7, 7, 8 and 1418 + 8570 gives 8, 8, 9, 9 — so a pupil could clear this whole set without ever carrying.
